text:
Timeline_ 2 days
Scope_ canvas, MCP server, mascots

Project_ Agent Canvas
Designed and built by_ Vignesh Murali

Agent Canvas is a drag-and-drop workspace for Claude agents and subagents. Workflows are drawn, checked and exported to run in your own Claude Code, and Claude can read and edit them over MCP. Every agent has a mascot that reacts to its checks.
modules.alt: Agent Canvas hero: where agent workflows become visible, with stats for 21 agents in the lobby, 10 MCP tools, 13 tests passing and 6 mascot species.

modules.name: 02 At a glance
heading: One canvas.
Every agent.
Two days.
modules.lede: No backend and no shared login: workflows live in the browser and run in each person's own Claude session.
text: No backend and no shared login: workflows live in the browser and run in each person's own Claude session.
Pan, zoom, connect and group nodes, with undo and a minimap.
Find problems before anything runs, then export to Claude Code.
Claude reads and edits workflows; Figma nodes and FigJam export.
modules.alt: At a glance: one canvas for every agent, built in two days, covering drawing, checks and exports, and MCP and Figma connections.

modules.name: 03 Problem
heading: Workflows in prompts.
Rules in heads.
Nothing to review.
modules.lede: Multi-agent work is hard to share when the only record of it is a prompt.
text: Multi-agent work is hard to share when the only record of it is a prompt.
No way to see or check one
Hard to hand to a teammate
Exports and page files to share
Claude can read it over MCP
modules.alt: The problem: workflows lived in prompts and memory; a before and after comparison with one Agent Canvas.

modules.name: 04 Process
heading: Draw it.
Check it.
Connect it.
modules.lede: Each layer was shipped and tested before the next was added.
text: Each layer was shipped and tested before the next was added.
Validation for cycles and missing tasks
Runbook, agent installer and page files
A static site; work stays in the browser.
Each person uses their own Anthropic key.
Workflows are validated and exported, not run.
The MCP server can drop its write tools.
modules.alt: Process in three phases, the canvas, trust and connect, plus four principles from no backend to a read-only option.

modules.name: 05 What we built
heading: What we built.
A canvas, a server,
and a crew.
text: Six species. Eyes follow the pointer, a poke makes them hop, and their mood follows the node's checks.
Reads, validates and edits workflow files, and never runs them. Ten tools and ten evaluation questions.
A Figma node in the workflow, and Share to FigJam turns a workflow into a diagram.
modules.alt: What we built: an example workflow from user brief through planner, design check and builder to human approval, with notes on mascots, the MCP server and Figma.

modules.name: 06 Today
heading: What it does
today.
Merged, and honest.
text: evaluation questions for the MCP server
Running workflows from the canvas, live multi-user editing, and discovery of your real Claude Code agents. The lobby is still sample data.
modules.alt: Result today: 21 agents in the lobby, 10 MCP tools, 13 tests passing and 10 evaluation questions, with a list of what is not built yet.
